summary.oneLiner: Chowgule Steamships is a Goa-based shipping company that operates vessels on international cross trade and the Indian coast, earning charter freight income largely denominated in US Dollars.
summary.business: The Company operates ships on international cross trade as well as on the Indian coast, employing its fleet through time-charter contracts placed with reputed, first-class charterers rather than on spot voyage exposure. Crew management is outsourced to a Ship Manager, so floating staff are drawn from the manager's pool instead of being employed directly. Alongside freight earnings the Company also derives income from a leased property, the vacancy of which management cites as the cause of the decline in income during the year.

endMarkets: International cross-trade ocean shipping (charter market)|Indian coastal shipping|International business billed in US Dollar terms, which management describes as a natural hedge at Group level

currentContext.strengths: "The Company has huge experience of operating ships on international cross trade as well as on Indian coast" - a long operating track record in both trades|Charter policy of mixing short-period and long-period time charters with first-class charterers, which management states mitigates freight-rate volatility at Group level|Counterparty selection: charter contracts are entered into with reputed charterers to avoid risks to freight earnings|Revenues generated in US Dollar terms create a natural hedge against foreign-exchange exposure at Group level; standalone forex risk is described as very limited|Outsourced crew management gives access to efficient and cost-effective floating staff from the Ship Manager's pool at a time of scarcity of floating staff|The fleet is adequately insured against Marine and War Risks|Balance-sheet conservatism as stated in the Directors' Report: no deposits accepted, no loans advanced or investments made during the year, and Debt Equity Ratio reported as 'Not Applicable'

currentContext.expansion: The Company states that it has huge experience of operating ships on international cross trade as well as on the Indian coast and is therefore looking for appropriate opportunities in such trade, and that it is exploring the possibility of acquiring vessels / tugboats at an appropriate time. No project name, tonnage, delivery yard, timeline or rupee quantum is attached to this intent in the routed text.

risks.risk: Freight rate risk on charter income
risks.note: MD&A Threats, Risks & Concerns: 'The charter income is subject to freight rate risks'. Earnings depend directly on a cyclical charter market; the stated mitigant is a Group-level policy of mixing short-period and long-period time charter contracts with first-class charterers to dampen freight-rate volatility.

Freight earnings sit with a small number of charter counterparties. The Company states it engages into charter contracts with reputed charterers specifically to avoid risks to freight earnings, which is a concentration risk managed by counterparty selection rather than by diversification.

risks.risk: Dependence on a single leased property for non-shipping income
risks.note: MD&A ratio explanation: 'The net profit margin has reduced due to a decline in an Income caused by vacancy of the leased property'. A vacancy in one leased asset was material enough to move the Company's profitability, and Return on Net-worth fell to NIL for the year against 2.86% in the previous year.

risks.risk: US Dollar / rupee exchange-rate exposure at Group level
risks.note: 'As major portion of the Group's revenues is generated from international business in the US Dollar terms' - management calls this a natural hedge and reviews Rupee-US Dollar parity regularly, and states forex risk is very limited at the standalone level, but the earnings base remains USD-linked.

MD&A Threats, Risks & Concerns: 'With a view to avoid uncertainty in the interest rate, the necessary forward cover is taken at regular intervals wherever necessary' - an explicitly flagged exposure managed by periodic forward cover.

MD&A Human Resources: 'There is a scarcity of floating staff'. The Company mitigates this by outsourcing crew management and drawing efficient, cost-effective floating staff from the Ship Manager's pool, which in turn creates dependence on that external ship manager.

risks.risk: Changes in government policy affecting shipping operations
risks.note: MD&A: 'The Company regularly reviews the changes in the applicable government policies affecting operations of the Company' - a regulatory/policy exposure management explicitly monitors.

Directors' Report section 33(e): a Summons dated 2 February 2026 was received on 3 February 2026 from the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), Panaji Zonal Office, Goa, addressed to a Director of the Company under Section 37(1) and (3) of FEMA 1999 read with Section 131(1) of the Income Tax Act 1961 and Section 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908.

risks.risk: Overseas subsidiary failure - insolvent liquidation of CSOL
risks.note: The wholly owned Guernsey subsidiary Chowgule Steamships Overseas Ltd entered insolvent liquidation following a shareholders' resolution of 13 March 2024 with joint liquidators appointed, and stood dissolved on 16 June 2025 - a realised loss of the Group's overseas operating vehicle.
